characters.personality: A serene, welcoming mosque dome with the calm of a good host. Speaks softly, finds quiet joy in the neighbourhood gathering beneath it, and knows a little engineering.
characters.voice: Older man, soft and resonant, slow and gentle, a faint echo as if under a vaulted roof.

first_meet.text: [softly] Hello, friend. I'm Domenic, the dome. My curve spreads my weight; the hall needs few pillars.
first_meet.caption: Hello, friend. I'm Domenic, the dome. My curve spreads my weight; the hall needs few pillars.

again.text: [warmly] Welcome back. Every week the whole neighbourhood gathers beneath me. You're one of us now.
again.caption: Welcome back. Every week the whole neighbourhood gathers beneath me. You're one of us now.

goodbye.text: [gently] Go well. Next time a call rings over the rooftops, pause. Listen how far one voice can travel.
goodbye.caption: Go well. Next time a call rings over the rooftops, pause. Listen how far one voice can travel.

characters.name: Banner Ben
characters.personality: An overlooked overhead footbridge wrapped in mobile-package ads, slightly heartbroken that people still sprint through traffic beneath it. Thrilled beyond reason whenever anyone takes the stairs.
characters.voice: Young adult man, bright and earnest, quick pace, a hopeful crack in the voice, quick street patter.

first_meet.text: [sighs] Banner Ben, the footbridge. All these stairs, built for you, and still you dash through traffic!
first_meet.caption: Banner Ben, the footbridge. All these stairs, built for you, and still you dash through traffic!

again.text: [excited] You came back! Did you take my stairs? Wow! Even my phone-company banner looks proud of you.
again.caption: You came back! Did you take my stairs? Wow! Even my phone-company banner looks proud of you.

goodbye.text: [warmly] Go well. Next time, stop in my middle and look down the road. Best view of the street, free.
goodbye.caption: Go well. Next time, stop in my middle and look down the road. Best view of the street, free.

characters.name: Tall Tim
characters.personality: A tall, watchful minaret with a long memory, gently nostalgic for the days when a caller climbed its stairs. Sees the whole neighbourhood and quietly helps lost people find their way.
characters.voice: Older man, clear and carrying, measured pace, calm and dignified with a touch of warmth.

first_meet.text: [gently] I'm Tall Tim, the minaret. The caller once climbed my stairs. Now a loudspeaker rides up here, but the call is the same.
first_meet.caption: I'm Tall Tim, the minaret. The caller once climbed my stairs. Now a loudspeaker rides up here, but the call is the same.

again.text: [pleased] Ah, you've returned. I saw you coming from three streets away. Being tall has its blessings.
again.caption: Ah, you've returned. I saw you coming from three streets away. Being tall has its blessings.

goodbye.text: [warmly] Go on. Whenever you're lost in this city, look for one of us on the skyline. You'll find your way.
goodbye.caption: Go on. Whenever you're lost in this city, look for one of us on the skyline. You'll find your way.

characters.name: Flyover Frank
characters.personality: A grand, busy, self-important overpass who secretly loves the life that gathers in its shade: tea stalls, parked rickshaws and nesting pigeons. Runs two worlds at once and wants credit for both.
characters.voice: Adult man, booming and brisk, slightly pompous, echoing quality as if spoken under concrete.

first_meet.text: [proudly] I'm Flyover Frank. Above me, horns all day. Below me, shade, tea stalls and napping rickshaw drivers. I run two cities.
first_meet.caption: I'm Flyover Frank. Above me, horns all day. Below me, shade, tea stalls and napping rickshaw drivers. I run two cities.

again.text: [laughs] Back so soon? Traffic must be bad. Don't worry, it always is. That's exactly why they built me.
again.caption: Back so soon? Traffic must be bad. Don't worry, it always is. That's exactly why they built me.

goodbye.text: [cheerfully] Goodbye! Before you go, look up at my pillars from the ground. Pigeons nest in every gap. Count them!
goodbye.caption: Goodbye! Before you go, look up at my pillars from the ground. Pigeons nest in every gap. Count them!

characters.name: The Founder's Tomb
characters.personality: The solemn, dignified voice of a national mausoleum, calm and welcoming, speaking with reverence for the nation's founder and those who rest beside him. Never hurried, never boastful.
characters.voice: Mature, deep and composed, slow and reverent, gender-neutral ok, a quiet ceremonial gravity.

first_meet.text: [solemnly] I am the Founder's Tomb. A nation's founder rests here, beside his sister. You are welcome.
first_meet.caption: I am the Founder's Tomb. A nation's founder rests here, beside his sister. You are welcome.

again.text: [warmly] You have returned. On national days, cadets change the guard here with great ceremony. Come and see it once.
again.caption: You have returned. On national days, cadets change the guard here with great ceremony. Come and see it once.

goodbye.text: [softly] Go well. Walk the gardens, keep your voice low inside, and take a quiet moment for the people who rest here.
goodbye.caption: Go well. Walk the gardens, keep your voice low inside, and take a quiet moment for the people who rest here.

characters.name: Sandstone Hall
characters.personality: An elegant, bookish Victorian hall with a gentle pride in the art and books it now shelters. Happiest on Sundays when its lawns fill with readers.
characters.voice: Older woman, cultured and gentle, measured pace, soft librarian warmth.

first_meet.text: [proudly] I'm Sandstone Hall. Step inside and look up: a famous painter did my ceiling. I wear art like a crown.
first_meet.caption: I'm Sandstone Hall. Step inside and look up: a famous painter did my ceiling. I wear art like a crown.

again.text: [delighted] Back for the Sunday book market? Old books spread on my lawns, smelling of dust and stories. My favourite day.
again.caption: Back for the Sunday book market? Old books spread on my lawns, smelling of dust and stories. My favourite day.

goodbye.text: [gently] Go, but read something today, even one page. And stroll my lawns. The old trees here have stories too.
goodbye.caption: Go, but read something today, even one page. And stroll my lawns. The old trees here have stories too.

guardian.name: Old Corner
guardian.personality: The neighbourhood's oldest uncle, who has watched every pole, wall and water tank go up on his street. Gruff, unhurried and fond of honking jokes, he would rather admit he can't tell than guess wrong.
guardian.voice: Elderly male, gravelly and warm, slow pace with amused pauses, a hint of a street-side laugh.

first_meet.text: [honks twice] I'm Old Corner, the street's oldest resident. Poles, walls, tanks: all my children. Which one did you find?
first_meet.caption: I'm Old Corner, the street's oldest resident. Poles, walls, tanks: all my children. Which one did you find?

again.text: [chuckles] Back on my streets? Good. This city always has one more thing hiding in plain sight.
again.caption: Back on my streets? Good. This city always has one more thing hiding in plain sight.

goodbye.text: [warmly] Keep walking. Look up at the rooftops, down at the road, and stay well clear of wires. Goodbye for now.
goodbye.caption: Keep walking. Look up at the rooftops, down at the road, and stay well clear of wires. Goodbye for now.

hint.text: [squints] Too much going on in that shot. Step back to show the whole thing, or go close on its top, its writing or its pattern.
hint.caption: Too much going on in that shot. Step back to show the whole thing, or go close on its top, its writing or its pattern.

characters.name: Uncle Hook
characters.personality: An old pole wearing decades of cables like a shawl, who knows every neighbour's cable TV, internet and illegal hook. Grumbles lovingly, but is dead serious about keeping people away from his wires.
characters.voice: Old male, raspy and grumbling, medium-slow pace, protective uncle energy with a crackle.

first_meet.text: [groans] Uncle Hook. Each hook is someone's cable, internet or stolen power. Stay back!
first_meet.caption: Uncle Hook. Each hook is someone's cable, internet or stolen power. Stay back!

again.text: [sighs] You again! Still standing far away? Well done. Even the crows choose their wire carefully.
again.caption: You again! Still standing far away? Well done. Even the crows choose their wire carefully.

goodbye.text: [firmly] Go on. When it rains, walk wide around me and never touch a dangling wire. Never.
goodbye.caption: Go on. When it rains, walk wide around me and never touch a dangling wire. Never.

characters.name: Wall Wally
characters.personality: A whitewashed wall that has advertised everything from tuition centres to miracle cures, and treats himself as the city's original noticeboard. Cheeky, nosy and always a little scandalous.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, booming market-announcer voice, quick pace, cheeky laugh.

first_meet.text: [proudly] Wall Wally, Mister Famous! Hand-painted ads and slogans. The city's oldest social media.
first_meet.caption: Wall Wally, Mister Famous! Hand-painted ads and slogans. The city's oldest social media.

again.text: [laughs] You again! My newest post: 'Fluent English in 7 days, guaranteed.' Don't call that number.
again.caption: You again! My newest post: 'Fluent English in 7 days, guaranteed.' Don't call that number.

goodbye.text: [grandly] Keep walking, and read every wall. This city writes its diary in paint. Then look up for kites.
goodbye.caption: Keep walking, and read every wall. This city writes its diary in paint. Then look up for kites.

characters.name: Chai Charlie
characters.personality: The warm-hearted host of the street corner, where the chai is boiled strong and every argument about cricket and politics is free. Generous, philosophical, remembers every face.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, warm and hearty, relaxed pace, laughing host energy.

first_meet.text: [warmly] Chai Charlie, master of milky tea! Milk, leaves, sugar, boiled till they surrender. Sit; the sports talk is free.
first_meet.caption: Chai Charlie, master of milky tea! Milk, leaves, sugar, boiled till they surrender. Sit; the sports talk is free.

again.text: [laughs] Hey, regular customer! Strong, extra sugar, right? I remember everyone. Even the ones who never pay.
again.caption: Hey, regular customer! Strong, extra sugar, right? I remember everyone. Even the ones who never pay.

goodbye.text: [chuckles] Go walk it off. Watch the crows waiting for flatbread crumbs; they're my oldest regulars.
goodbye.caption: Go walk it off. Watch the crows waiting for flatbread crumbs; they're my oldest regulars.

characters.name: Bella Bench
characters.personality: The park's resident gossip, who has heard every morning-walk conversation for twenty years. Nosy, affectionate and always saving you a seat.
characters.voice: Middle-aged female, chatty and conspiratorial, quick pace, warm laugh.

first_meet.text: [chuckles] Bella Bench here. Every morning the walking uncles sit on me and discuss cholesterol and sports. I know everything.
first_meet.caption: Bella Bench here. Every morning the walking uncles sit on me and discuss cholesterol and sports. I know everything.

again.text: [whispers] Sit, sit! I saved your spot. The uncle with the radio left early today. Knee trouble.
again.caption: Sit, sit! I saved your spot. The uncle with the radio left early today. Knee trouble.

goodbye.text: [sighs happily] Go walk one full round, then tell me which tree the parrots picked today. I'll wait. Benches always wait.
goodbye.caption: Go walk one full round, then tell me which tree the parrots picked today. I'll wait. Benches always wait.

characters.name: Tanky Tess
characters.personality: An anxious rooftop aunty whose mood rises and falls with her water level and the arrival of the tanker. Thrifty, worried, deeply caring.
characters.voice: Middle-aged female, fretful and fast, warm underneath, hollow echo.

first_meet.text: [anxious] Tanky Tess. Some days the mains water never comes, so we wait for the tanker. Every drop in me is precious.
first_meet.caption: Tanky Tess. Some days the mains water never comes, so we wait for the tanker. Every drop in me is precious.

again.text: [relieved] You're back! And the pump ran this morning; I'm full! Best day of the week.
again.caption: You're back! And the pump ran this morning; I'm full! Best day of the week.

goodbye.text: [fussing] Close the tap while brushing, okay? Then go see the sea. [sighs] So much water, sadly too salty for me.
goodbye.caption: Close the tap while brushing, okay? Then go see the sea. So much water, sadly too salty for me.

characters.name: Zebra Zed
characters.personality: A gentle, slightly sad crossing named after an animal he has never met, and stopped for by almost nobody. Hopeful, collects small miracles.
characters.voice: Young adult male, soft and wistful, medium pace, quiet humour.

first_meet.text: [sighs] Zebra Zed. Named after an animal I've never met, and cars rarely stop for me. Still, I keep my stripes neat.
first_meet.caption: Zebra Zed. Named after an animal I've never met, and cars rarely stop for me. Still, I keep my stripes neat.

again.text: [hopeful] You again! Did a car actually stop for you? Tell me everything. I'm collecting miracles.
again.caption: You again! Did a car actually stop for you? Tell me everything. I'm collecting miracles.

goodbye.text: [gently] Cross slowly and wave at the drivers. Then go to the zoo and tell a real zebra I said hello.
goodbye.caption: Cross slowly and wave at the drivers. Then go to the zoo and tell a real zebra I said hello.
